topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and sources of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations produce cancer through clonal evolution and why some cells and individuals are more susceptible to that process.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposure to cancer risk against competing explanations based on chance and inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental agents damage DNA and generate mutations, with their effects shaped by the body's handling of those agents.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a subsequent growth-promoting environment for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Tissue and life-stage susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on the exposed tissue's biological context and conclude by placing that specificity within the mechanisms already discussed.

topics.label: Tracing carcinogen exposure through mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how patterns in cancer genomes can provide evidence of prior exposure to particular carcinogens.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the available approaches to establishing carcinogenic potential and the limitations of the evidence they produce.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment through the everyday balance of risks and benefits.
